title: A form validator
description:
Validate sign-up data and report every problem at once with your own error class.

```
validate({ name: "", email: "ada@", age: 12 })
-> throws ValidationError with problems:
   name: is required
   email: is not an email address
   age: must be 13 or older
```
hints: `atLeast(13)` returns a rule, so `atLeast` is a function that makes functions (lesson 2.04): `` const atLeast = min => value => (value < min ? `must be ${min} or older` : null); ``
For each field, `rules[field].map(rule => rule(data[field])).find(m => m !== null)` is its first problem, or `undefined`.
requirements: `class ValidationError extends Error` with a `problems` array of `{ field, message }`.
Rules come from a table: `{ name: [required], email: [required, isEmail], age: [isNumber, atLeast(13)] }`; each rule returns a message or `null`.
Stop at the first failing rule of each field, but check every field.
Valid data returns `true`. A caller catches the error with `instanceof ValidationError`.
stretch: Let a rule see all the data, so "repeat password" can compare two fields.
